full_text_en:
Huang Guangna v. Haikou Dongliang Industrial Co., Ltd. and Hainan Branch of Guangdong Yangjiang Jian'an Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a commercial housing sales contract

[Ruling Summary]

I. The registered owner of the real property in dispute in a case has a legal interest in the outcome of the case and may be joined as a third party in the case.

II. If a major shareholder of a party acquires the subject matter of the dispute during the course of the litigation but does not participate in the proceedings as a third party, and after the judgment takes effect, files a third-party revocation action, the court shall presume that the shareholder was aware of the case circumstances. It is consistent with common sense and business conventions that the shareholder's failure to participate was not due to reasons not attributable to himself or herself. The third-party revocation action brought by the aforementioned major shareholder does not meet the conditions for filing a lawsuit and shall be dismissed by ruling.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2015) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 37

Appellant (first-instance plaintiff): Huang Guangna, female, Han ethnicity, residing in Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Agent ad litem: Xuan Liqin, female, Han ethnicity, residing at Hainan University, Haikou City, Hainan Province. A citizen recommended by the villagers' committee to which Huang Guangna belongs.

Huang Guangna, in the dispute with Haikou Dongliang Industrial Co., Ltd. and the Hainan Branch of Guangdong Yangjiang Jian'an Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yangjiang Company) over a commercial housing sales contract, appealed against the civil ruling (2015) Qiong Li Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Hainan High People's Court to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted a trial, which has now concluded.

On August 18, 2014, Huang Guangna filed a civil lawsuit with the Hainan High People's Court, alleging: On October 31, 2012, Huang Guangna signed a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Haikou Dongliang Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongliang Company), agreeing that Huang Guangna would purchase Room 101 on the first floor of Huayuan Building, located at No. 97-1 Longkun South Road, Haikou City, Hainan Province, with a total construction area of 1320.6 square meters, at a unit price of RMB 21,250 per square meter. After the contract was signed, Dongliang Company registered the commercial housing sales contract and applied for advance notice registration of the house for Huang Guangna in accordance with the contract. Huang Guangna paid the full purchase price of RMB 28,062,750 to Dongliang Company as agreed, including RMB 16,062,750 paid by herself and RMB 12,000,000 obtained by mortgaging the said property to Ping An Bank Co., Ltd., Haikou Branch (hereinafter referred to as Ping An Bank). Huang Guangna has obtained ownership of the house through assignment, and the property is currently rented out to others for use.

In 2012, the Hainan Branch of Guangdong Yangjiang Jian'an Group Co., Ltd. and Dongliang Company filed a lawsuit in the Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province over a construction contract dispute, and the subject matter of the dispute in that case involved the house owned by Huang Guangna. Although Dongliang Company submitted evidence to the court within the first-instance evidence submission period that the house in question had been sold to Huang Guangna and all legal requirements for the real estate transaction had been completed, after two trials, neither Huang Guangna as the owner nor Ping An Bank as the mortgagee was aware of the existence of the lawsuit. Neither the first-instance nor the second-instance court added the two interested parties as third parties to the proceedings. Moreover, the second-instance court, without examining the actual ownership of the house in question, issued the civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7 on June 26, 2014, awarding part of the property rights of the house in question to Yangjiang Company, which seriously infringed on the legitimate rights and interests of the owner Huang Guangna. In accordance with Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 75 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 8 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 37 and 39 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, Huang Guangna now requests the cancellation of the civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7 of the Hainan High People's Court to lawfully protect her legitimate rights and interests.

The Hainan High People's Court held that: First, in accordance with Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a third party with an independent claim and a third party without an independent claim who did not participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to themselves, but has evidence proving that part or all of the content of a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation statement is erroneous, thereby damaging their civil rights and interests, may, within six months from the date they know or should have known that their civil rights and interests have been damaged, file a third-party revocation action with the people's court that rendered the judgment, ruling, or mediation statement. This provision establishes the right of a third party to file a revocation action. Because a third-party revocation action seeks to revoke an effective judgment, ruling, or mediation statement, its consequence will directly affect the res judicata of the effective adjudication. Therefore, the law strictly stipulates the conditions for the subject of a third-party revocation action: the plaintiff filing the third-party revocation action must be a third party, including a third party with an independent claim and a third party without an independent claim, and the plaintiff filing the third-party revocation action can only be a third party in the original lawsuit. In the civil lawsuit that Huang Guangna seeks to revoke, namely the civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7 of the Hainan High People's Court, the first-instance plaintiff Yangjiang Company filed a lawsuit with the Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province on September 18, 2012, and the court accepted the case on September 20, 2012. However, Huang Guangna signed the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Dongliang Company on October 31, 2012, which was more than one month after the case was accepted. Therefore, at the time the original lawsuit was formed, Huang Guangna was not yet a third party in the original lawsuit and did not have the subject qualification to file a third-party revocation action. Second, one of the conditions for filing a third-party revocation action is that the third party did not participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to themselves. The industrial and commercial registration records of Dongliang Company show that from September 17, 2009, to January 27, 2014, Huang Guangna was a shareholder holding 50% of the shares of Dongliang Company, and up to the time of filing this lawsuit, Huang Guangna still held 25% of the shares of Dongliang Company. In the first and second instances of the civil lawsuit (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7, Dongliang Company submitted to the court evidence that Huang Guangna had purchased the house in question. As a shareholder holding 50% of the shares of the company, Huang Guangna should have known the litigation circumstances of that case. Moreover, up to the time of filing this lawsuit, Huang Guangna failed to provide evidence to prove that she did not participate in the proceedings of that case due to reasons not attributable to herself. Therefore, Huang Guangna's filing of this lawsuit also does not meet the acceptance conditions for a third-party revocation action. In summary, in accordance with Articles 56 and 123 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled that Huang Guangna's lawsuit would not be accepted.

Huang Guangna refused to accept the above ruling and appealed to this Court on the grounds that the ruling was unclear in fact finding and erroneous in law application, requesting that the first-instance ruling be revoked and the case be remanded to the first-instance court for trial. The main reasons were: First, the appellant is the owner of the property involved in the civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7, and the outcome of that judgment damages her legitimate rights and interests; therefore, she should be a third party in the lawsuit involved in that judgment. Second, as a shareholder of Dongliang Company, the appellant has the right to acquire the property rights of the house in question in accordance with the law. The first-instance ruling's inference, based on her status as a shareholder of the company, that she knew the litigation circumstances of Dongliang Company in the above case lacks evidence. This case meets the acceptance conditions for a third-party revocation action.

This Court holds: The issues in dispute in this case are, first, whether Huang Guangna can be a third party in the dispute between Yangjiang Company and Dongliang Company over a construction contract; and second, whether Huang Guangna's failure to participate in the aforementioned lawsuit can be attributed to herself.

Regarding the issue of whether Huang Guangna can be a third party in the dispute between Yangjiang Company and Dongliang Company over a construction contract. In accordance with Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, third parties in civil proceedings include persons who have an independent claim to the subject matter of the lawsuit, and persons who, although they do not have such a claim, have a legal interest in the outcome of the case. In the dispute between Yangjiang Company and Dongliang Company over a construction contract, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province, in its second-instance civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7, ordered Dongliang Company to deliver 334 square meters of the first floor of Huayuan Building in question to Yangjiang Company and assist in handling the property transfer procedures. However, in this case, Huang Guangna claims that she has purchased 1320 square meters of the first floor of Huayuan Building from Dongliang Company and has completed the transfer procedures. Therefore, the final judgment result of the aforementioned lawsuit between Yangjiang Company and Dongliang Company affects Huang Guangna's rights to the property in question, and she should be a third party in that case.

Regarding the issue of whether Huang Guangna's failure to participate in the aforementioned lawsuit can be attributed to herself. Based on the facts found in the civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7 and the content of Huang Guangna's lawsuit in this case, she and Dongliang Company signed the sales contract for the house in question during the course of the lawsuit between Yangjiang Company and Dongliang Company. At that time, Huang Guangna was a shareholder holding 50% of the shares of Dongliang Company. Given that the outcome of the aforementioned lawsuit between Yangjiang Company and Dongliang Company would inevitably affect Huang Guangna's significant rights and interests, Huang Guangna failed to provide evidence to prove that, before filing this revocation action, the conditions under which she learned of the aforementioned second-instance judgment result were different from those under which she would have known the entire course of the lawsuit. The first-instance court, based on Huang Guangna's shareholder status, her shareholding ratio at the time, and the relationship between the signing of the house sales contract and the time the previous lawsuit was filed, inferred that Huang Guangna knew about the previous lawsuit. This is consistent with common sense and general corporate business decision-making practices. The first-instance ruling correctly determined that Huang Guangna should have known the litigation circumstances of the previous lawsuit and that she could not prove that she did not participate in the lawsuit due to reasons not attributable to herself. Therefore, the lawsuit she filed does not meet the acceptance conditions for a third-party revocation action as provided in Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

In summary, the first-instance ruling's determination that Huang Guangna was not a third party in the case involved in the civil judgment (2014) Qiong Huan Min Zhong Zi No. 7 is improper, and this Court hereby corrects it. The appellant Huang Guangna's argument that she did not participate in the aforementioned lawsuit due to reasons not attributable to herself lacks evidence support and cannot be established. In accordance with Articles 56, 170(1)(a), and 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

Appeal rejected and the original ruling affirmed.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Yang Guoxiang

Acting Judge: Zhang Na

Acting Judge: Li Zhenhua

October 16, 2015

Yang Guoxiang, Senior Judge, born in 1962, Bachelor of Laws, served as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2007.
